readings.title: A timetable that learners could keep
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: When the Elm Adult Centre opened its evening language course, every lesson lasted two hours. The timetable looked efficient, but several learners worked changing shifts and could not arrive on time. The centre first considered recording every lesson. Interviews revealed a different problem: learners wanted opportunities to ask questions, not simply more recordings to watch alone. The revised course kept one weekly discussion and added two short independent tasks. Learners could complete those tasks at any time before Sunday. Attendance at discussions improved, although the total amount of study remained similar. Tutors now ask about work schedules before publishing each term's timetable. They judge a useful course partly by whether people can continue attending it.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: The quiet corner experiment
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A railway waiting hall introduced a quiet corner behind a low wooden screen. The station did not ban conversation across the whole building. Instead, signs asked visitors in that corner to silence devices and take calls elsewhere. During the first week, some passengers thought the seats cost extra because the space looked different. Staff added a clear notice saying that all passengers could use them without payment. Complaints then declined. The corner was particularly popular with people reading work documents while waiting. However, staff kept a wide opening so travellers could see platform announcements. The experiment showed that a small change to a public space can help, provided its purpose and conditions are easy to understand.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Measuring progress in short notes
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Rina used to count the hours she spent studying English after work. A long session felt successful even when she could not explain what she had learned. Her tutor suggested a different record: after each session, write one sentence about a new skill and one question that remained. At first, Rina's notes were vague. Gradually, she began recording specific achievements, such as understanding the reason in a short announcement. The questions also helped her choose material for the next session. She still noted study time, but no longer treated it as the only measure of progress. Looking back over a month of notes made small improvements visible and helped her identify topics that needed further practice.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Seats shared between two organisations
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A neighbourhood office was empty most evenings, while a nearby training charity could not afford a larger classroom. They agreed to share the office three evenings a week. The arrangement required more than handing over a key. Confidential papers had to be locked away, desks returned to their daytime positions, and cleaning duties assigned. A short checklist was placed beside the exit. The charity appointed one person to check it after every session. After two months, both organisations reported few difficulties. They decided to continue but reserved one evening each month for office maintenance. Sharing made better use of an existing room without assuming that every unused hour should automatically become a teaching hour.

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
A useful study plan leaves room for ordinary life. Adults may have to change their plans when work becomes busy or a family member needs help. Missing one session does not make the whole plan worthless. What matters is knowing how to return to it. A small task that can be finished today often provides a better starting point than an ambitious promise for next month.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 注意leave room for的比喻意义、what matters主语从句以及最后一句比较结构。
translation.referenceAnswer: 一份实用的学习计划会为日常生活留出余地。当工作变得忙碌或家人需要帮助时，成年人可能不得不调整计划。错过一次学习并不意味着整个计划毫无价值。重要的是知道如何重新回到计划中。与其对下个月作出宏大的承诺，不如完成今天能做完的一项小任务，这往往是更好的起点。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English to the manager of an adult learning centre. Suggest one change to evening study facilities, explain how it would help working learners, and propose a practical way to try it.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 建议须具体说明设施改变、受益人群和试行办法；保持礼貌书信语气。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Dear Manager,
I am writing to suggest a small quiet study area for learners who come directly from work. At present, the shared hall is useful for conversation, but it is difficult to concentrate there when several groups are meeting.
A quiet area would give learners somewhere to read notes or prepare questions before class. It would be especially helpful for people who do not have a suitable desk at home. I suggest using the smaller room on Tuesday and Thursday evenings for a one-month trial. Clear signs could explain that phone calls should be taken outside. Learners could leave short comments after using the room.
These comments would help you decide whether to continue the arrangement. Thank you for considering this suggestion.
Yours sincerely,
A course member
